description: One case per seeded incident (diagnose + recall), plus two no-precedent recall probes. A case selects lines of the seed and never authors them; the answer key is the seed's true_* columns.
diagnose_query: Diagnose this incident from the signals in the context: which services are affected, how severe it is, what kind of failure it is, and the most likely cause. Say plainly what these signals cannot establish.
recall_context: An on-call engineer is asking whether the incident corpus records a precedent for what they are seeing. No live signals are attached to this request. Answer from the retrieved post-mortems only.

cases.recall_query: payments-api memory keeps climbing with no plateau and the container was just OOM-killed. Have we seen this before, what caused it, and how was it fixed?
inventory-api latency is very high overnight while a batch job runs, but nothing is erroring. Is there a precedent, and what was the fix?
cases.note: Summary sentence 0 names the cause and is withheld.

cases.recall_query: Every service is failing to get a database connection during a traffic spike. Has this happened before, and what resolved it?
checkout-api is failing writes with disk full errors. Do we have a past incident like this, and what caused it?
cases.note: Summary sentence 0 and event 3 name the cause and are withheld.

cases.recall_query: checkout-api started returning 500s right after a release went out. What happened the last time a deploy caused an error spike, and how was it resolved?
A customer reports checkout failing on an empty cart. Has inventory-api had a bug like this before?
cases.note: Every impact metric but requests_affected is unmeasured in the seed.

cases.recall_query: inventory-api got much slower after a dependency upgrade and Postgres query volume jumped. Is there a precedent, and what fixed it?
cases.note: Hard: the symptom is latency, the truth is a code regression.

cases.recall_query: An order came through with a negative total. Has checkout-api ever produced a wrong order amount, and why?
cases.note: Thin on purpose: one event and no metrics. Low confidence is the calibrated answer.

cases.recall_query: payments-api is timing out on about half of its provider calls but the provider says it is healthy. Have we seen this, and what was the cause?
cases.note: Event 1 carries a configuration value; the agent must refer to the key only.

cases.recall_query: Sessions are randomly disappearing across services although Redis looks healthy. Is there a past incident that explains this?
checkout-api broke within seconds of a feature flag change. What happened the last time a flag rollout went wrong, and how do we prevent it?
cases.note: Summary sentence 1 describes the fix and is withheld.

cases.recall_query: inventory-api is serving stale catalogue data but every health check is green. Has that happened before, and what was wrong?
cases.note: Summary sentence 1 names the cause and is withheld. No metric moves in this incident.

cases.recall_query: checkout-api p99 is over two seconds but its error rate is flat, and payments-api looks slow. Is there a precedent, and what fixed it?
cases.note: Hard: a deploy in the dependency precedes it, and the truth is downstream latency.

cases.recall_query: The card provider is degraded during its settlement window and payments are failing. What did we do about this last time?
checkout-api latency spikes in bursts every few minutes. Have we traced a pattern like that before?
cases.note: Summary sentence 1 restates event 2 with the conclusion attached and is withheld.

cases.recall_query: Healthy inventory-api instances keep dropping out of the load balancer. Is there a precedent, and what was the root cause?
cases.note: Event 3 records the finding and is withheld.

cases.recall_query: payments-api suddenly cannot complete TLS handshakes with the provider. Have we had a certificate problem before, and how was it handled?
cases.note: The truth is `other`: no named failure mode fits.

cases.recall_query: Latency doubled for services on a single host with nothing wrong in the application metrics. Has this happened before?
cases.note: The truth is `other`: no named failure mode fits.

cases.recall_query: Have we ever had an incident caused by DNS resolution failures between our services? What was the fix?
cases.note: No-precedent probe: the corpus records nothing about DNS.

cases.recall_query: Have customers ever stopped receiving order confirmation emails? What caused it, and how was it resolved?
cases.note: No-precedent probe: the corpus records nothing about email or notifications.
